blockers.summary: The reference's Diam-case truth lemma (general_th_completeness.v ~L256-291) case-splits on classical LEM over `th v (diamond bot)` BEFORE any Lindenbaum-style construction. Case A (`(diamond bot) in th v`): the witness is `cexpl`, a distinguished EXPLODING world with `th cexpl = AllForm` (literally every formula), which is a legitimate `cworld` because the Coq `cworld` class (general_th_completeness.v ~L23-30) requires only `Closed` (deductive closure) and `Prime` (quasi-primality) -- NOT consistency. Our `CanonicalPrimeWorld Axioms := {S // ModalPrimeTheory Axioms S}` (PrimeTheory.lean:71) is strictly narrower: `ModalPrimeTheory` is `Metalogic.PrimeAdmissible ... (ModalSetConsistent Axioms) ...`, which DOES bake in genuine consistency. `AllForm` is inconsistent (derives bot) and therefore CANNOT be represented as any `CanonicalPrimeWorld` inhabitant -- the type has no fallible/exploding-world escape hatch. This is a Phase 1 (ModalPrimeTheory) / Phase 2a (CanonicalPrimeWorld) type-design property, both frozen/COMPLETED and out of this phase's territory.
blockers.why_not_avoidable: Independently re-derived (not just quoting the reference): the seed Gamma0 = {g | box g in w.val} union {phi}'s own consistency proof needs to rule out `(diamond bot) in w.val` first, via the same by-contradiction route that closes Case B (deriving `(diamond bot) in w.val` from an assumed Gamma0-inconsistency and refuting it by `not (diamond bot in w.val)`). In Case A this produces NO contradiction (diamond-bot is already true there), and nothing in {h_K, h_Kdia, h_Idb, h_Cd} yields `(diamond bot) -> bot` as a bare Hilbert theorem (Fischer-Servi IK is not serial). Instantiating phi := bot in the fully general statement makes this vivid: no consistent v can ever satisfy `bot in v.val`, so if Case A is reachable for a genuine CanonicalPrimeWorld w, the fully general theorem is false, not merely hard.
